title: Partial model serve during canary swap due to staggered KV sync
creator: Ava Chen
summary: During a scheduled canary rollout of model v2026-03-08 to a subset of pods, we observed a partial serve situation where ~30% of requests in the canary cohort were routed to pods that had applied the new model metadata but had not completed KV cache synchronization. This produced inconsistent latency and formatting differences in responses. An attempted automatic rollback did not fully unpin the target version due to a concurrency bug, extending the window of degraded output for downstream customers.

impact: Customer-facing: Intermittent formatting/sequence anomalies and higher latency for some requests routed during the canary. Internal: false-positive health signals caused autoscaler churn on the canary pool. Measured impact: ~3.2k requests affected, 12% p95 latency increase in canary cohort, two customer tickets flagged within the hour.
root_cause: Primary: Canary rollout used the progressive-stagger orchestration without ensuring atomic commit between model metadata activation and KV cache warmup. Some nodes activated model metadata and started serving before KV cache sync completed. Secondary: Route translator had a concurrency edge where a rollback/unpin and a delayed health reconciliation could interleave, leaving some nodes logically pinned to the canary model while the control-plane believed the rollback completed.
contributing_factors:
1) rollout policy (progressive-stagger) lacked a preflight KV-warm precondition.
2) KV sync is asynchronous and not surfaced as part of the model activation state.
3) Route translator unpin API implementation allowed concurrent unpin calls without a compare-and-swap guard.
4) Observability dashboards did not expose per-node KV sync progress, only aggregate health metrics.
5) No automated canary gate for format/response-shape regressions (only latency/error-rate).
detection_and_response: Detected by alerting on tail latency and a new format-mismatch metric introduced last quarter. Oncall performed standard rollback via console. Rollback returned success but did not clear all pinned state; manual node drain and forced KV resync were used as remediation. Post-incident, we created a terse runbook for this failure mode and flagged the rollout service for a bugfix.
mitigation_now:
- Forced KV resync on affected nodes.
- Drained and replaced nodes with mismatched metadata.
- Scoped temporary safety: disable progressive-stagger for model rollouts >= 3GB unless KV preflight passes.
- Notified customers in impacted orgs and created a short status note in #incidents and customer support tickets.

postmortem_notes: This incident is similar in theme to previous rollout edge cases, but differs technically in that KV-caching was the missing synchronization primitive rather than a routing weight calculation bug. We should treat KV cache warmup as first-class state in the rollout protocol. The fix will change rollout semantics (adds a preflight block) which requires careful UX in Console and may affect rollout duration SLAs; Product has been looped in.
